title: Morse-Smale decomposition Phase A: diagnostic overlay
description:
Prior decomposition work (PATCH-11..21) treats feature edges as negative constraints and splits patch interiors with k-means/BFS heuristics. On the skull that produces patches crossing ridges and containing multiple teeth. The fundamental constraint the user pointed out is that a Coons patch is a taut cloth — wrinkles cannot live in the interior, so every local curvature extremum must be inside exactly one cell and every saddle/ridge must be on a cell boundary. This is the Morse-Smale complex (MSC) by definition.

Phase A is DIAGNOSTIC ONLY: compute the MSC on the skull using signed mean curvature as the Morse function, render its critical points (red=max, blue=min, yellow=saddle) and integral arcs (black lines) as an overlay. No change to SemanticPatchDecomposer behavior; only additive fields on DecompositionDiagnostics.

Goal: visually confirm MSC cells match anatomy (tooth tips → max, inter-tooth valleys → saddle, sockets → min) before building a real decomposer on top.

New class: MorseSmaleComplex.java with:
- classifyCriticalPoints via lower-link connectivity (Banchoff)
- persistence-pair + simplify (start simple: sort pairs by |ΔH|, cull bottom N%)
- steepest-ascent/descent arc tracing from saddles (reuse CrestLineDetector.traceOneDirection pattern but swap eigenvector alignment for H-gradient)

Diagnostic overlay uses the PATCH-17 depth-aware overlay infra for free.

Phase B (integration as parallel pipeline) will be PATCH-23 with its own plan file.

Reference: kitten-style MSC images (one cell per anatomical feature, cells topologically quadrilateral) and the 2024 Tsiapkolis-Bénard patch decomposition paper (hal-04620165) for a secondary "normal cone per patch" invariant that could refine cells later.
definition-of-done:
1. MorseSmaleComplex.compute(mesh, scalarField, persistenceFrac) runs on the skull.
2. DecompositionDiagnostics exposes critical points (typed max/min/saddle) and integral arcs.
3. PatchRenderer renders critical-point dots + arcs as an overlay through the depth-aware PATCH-17 path.
4. On voyage_skull_ref.obj: red dots at tooth tips, blue dots in sockets, yellow dots at inter-tooth valleys, arcs connect them forming visibly closed anatomical cells at a reasonable persistence threshold.
5. Does NOT change patch counts or flat-patch rendering (decomposer untouched).
testing-plan:
1. Headless VerifyMsc runner: decomposeWithDiagnostics on skull, dump critical-point counts and arc count, emit overlay PNG at zoom 2.5.
2. Visual inspect Right + 3/4 Front-R: confirm dot placement matches anatomy.
3. Tune persistenceFrac (0.05 → 0.1 → 0.2) and recapture PNGs.
4. Live viewer: load skull, cycle into new MSC shader mode, orbit 360° and verify depth-aware arcs.
